agree.reason: Marisol gets a direct answer on the late report: a named treasurer, a 30-day deadline and quarterly updates. She would still hesitate because the $4,500 yearly running cost has no stated funding source and reserves would fall to $11,000.

honest.reason: The writer correctly drops the doubling claim, but adds small unsupported details such as 'a short drive away' and 'not been able to solve any other way.'

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out 3,000 lb a month, up to a 50% seasonal increase, 72,000 lb a year and about 12% annually, and it presents the $18,000 match as more than a quarter of the van's cost.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative of continuing to turn down cold produce is described accurately, though the cost of doing nothing is stated only for one summer.

qualification.reason: The 'target, not a guarantee' hedge sets no pound figure to check against the quarterly reports and says nothing about what happens if it is missed, although the report deadline is concrete.

objections.reason: It fully answers the late-report concern, but it raises the $4,500 yearly cost without saying who pays it and leaves the thin reserve unaddressed.

fit.reason: It is a narrative of roughly 500 words with clear sections, but it leaves '[Food Bank Name]' as a placeholder even though the name was available.
